JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Sri.Mukeshkumar in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case is as under:
2. That, on 10-01-2023 at about 7-30 p.m, the deceased Mukesh Kumar was proceeding as a pillion rider in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-53/
HL-0719, on Bangaluru-Doddaballapura road, when they reached near Factory Circle, Bashettihalli, Kasaba Hobli, Doddaballapura Taluk, at that time rider of pulsar motor cycle bearing registration KA- 03/JP-8262 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, came at high speed and dashed against deceased motor cycle from behind.
Due to said impact, the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated that, immediately after the accident, injured/deceased was shifted to Government Hospital, Doddaballapura and died in the hospital during the course of treatment.
After, post mortem body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.

4. It is further stated that prior to the accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 27 Narayanaswami vs Krishna Kumar M.S on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76168043/
2 years and working as a flower decorator- cum-auto driver and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.

Due to untimely death of the deceased,
petitioners have put to untold misery, pain, shock and mental agony.
5. It is further stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of pulsar motor cycle bearing registration KA-03/JP- 8262.
Hence, jurisdictional Doddaballapura Rural Police have filed criminal case in Cr.No.15/2023 against rider of said vehicle.

Hence,
respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
6. In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, hence he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 & 3 were appeared through their respective counsel.
The respondent No.2 filed the written statement and inspite of sufficient time, the respondent No.3 did not file his written statement.
7. In the written statement respondent No.2 contended that, the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further it has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of pulsar motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03/JP- 8262 and restricted its liability subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is contended that, rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. to the said vehicle as on the date of the accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased only.

Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and expenses incurred towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased and also denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

8. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that, Mukesh kumar died due to the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 10.1.2023 at about 7.30 p.m. on near Factory Circle, Bashettihalli, Bengaluru- Doddaballapura Road, Doddaballapura Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Bajaj Pulsor motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03-JP-8262 in an actionable negligence?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate ?
From whom?
3) What order or award?

3 9.
In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.2 got examined herself as PW1 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.

The copy of the charge sheet marked with consent at Ex.P20.
10.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 did not adduce evidence on its behalf.
11. Heard the arguments of both the counsels.
Perused the materials available on record.

12. My findings to the above issues as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:
13.

It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the pulsar motor cycle bearing registration KA-03/JP-8262, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently Sri.Mukesh Kumar had succumbed to the injuries.
14. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

15. On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the rider of the offending vehicle in question.
16. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.2 by name Smt.Lakshmamma got examined herself as PW1.
In her examination-in-chief by way of affidavit, she has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of her oral evidence has relied upon police documents marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11 and Ex.P20.

17. On perusal of Ex.P1-copy of the F.I.R. Ex.P2-copy of the first information statement, Ex.P3 & 4 are copies of spot mahazar & seizure mahazar, Ex.P5-copy of spot sketch, Ex.P6 & Ex.P7- copies of IMV report, Ex.P8-inquest report, Ex.P9-copy of post mortem report, Ex.P10 & Ex.P11 are copies of notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act and reply to the said notice.
and Ex.P20-copy of charge sheet marked with consent.

18. In order to substantiate the case of the respondent No.2 has not examined either the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove that the accident has not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

19. PW1 was subjected for cross-examination at length, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.

Narayanaswami vs Krishna Kumar M.S on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76168043/
4 20.
In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-03-JP-82622 and in the said accident, Mukesh Kumar succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
21.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P12 to Ex.P19 Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased, D.L., SSLC marks card of the deceased and ration card and PAN cards, which have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak that the petitioners are the parents of the deceased 22.

Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the age particulars of the petitioners, mentioned in the cause title of the petition, reflected that, the petitioners No.1 & 2 in their middle age, lost their son, as well as the care from their son, who was the backbone of the family.
The respondents herein have not produced documents on record, to show the independent economic status of the petitioners, at the time of cross-examination of the PW1.
By taking into consideration of all these factors, along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were the dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
23. To prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident, the petitioners have placed notarized copyof SSLC marks card of the deceased, it is marked at Ex.P16.

On going through same,
the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 15.11.1994.
The said document remained unquestioned by the other side.
The alleged accident had occurred on 10.1.2023.
Hence, I am of the view that, as on the date of the accident, the deceased was aged about 29 years.

For his age,
multiplier '17' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma" Case.

24. In connection with the work of the deceased in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was working as Flower decorator and also working as Auto driver and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The petitioners have not placed any document to show the income of the petitioner.

Hence, it is apt to take the notional income, by looking into consideration of the year of accident along with other facts and circumstances of the case, as well as by looking in to the chart of the notional income of the Legal Services Authority.
Hence, the income of the deceased is considered as Rs.16,000/- p.m., for the year 2023, which will meet the ends of justice.

25. Another point tobe taken into consideration herein that as per the petition, the deceased was a bachelor, for deduction of the personal and living expenses, the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14 is to be considered.

Narayanaswami vs Krishna Kumar M.S on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76168043/
5 26.
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self- employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50- 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
27. Having considered the above as per law laid down in the above case.

In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, since the deceased was a bachelor,
deduction towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation is to be considered.
In the present case, deceased was aged about 29 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "17" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through main petition averments it is evident that, the deceased herein as on the date of the accident was not having permanent job.

As such by taking into consideration of the nature of the employment mentioned in the petition, I am of the view that, 40% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
And Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 40% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased, comes to (Rs.1,92,000+76,800)= Rs.2,68,800/-.
And 50% has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
Thus net loss income comes to Rs.1,34,400/- (Rs.2,68,800- Rs.1,34,400/-).
This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "17".

Which comes to Rs.22,84,800/-.
28.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following decision;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81.
National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others
, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz.,
loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-,

6 Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

29. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/-
each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 & 2 under the head loss of filial consortium.

. Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.24,05,800/-
(Rupees twenty four lakhs five thousand and eight hundred only), along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016, Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.

LIABILITY:-
32.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the Pulsar motor cycle bearing Narayanaswami vs Krishna Kumar M.S on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76168043/
7 registration No.KA-03-JP- 8262, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
33. As per the records insurance policy was valid from 26.3.2022 to 25.3.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 10.1.2023.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify the respondent No.3.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
34.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,05,800/- (Rupees twenty four lakhs five thousand and eight hundred only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.

Out of share amount of petitoner No.1 and 2, 40% of the amount together with interest shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of of the amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,05,800/- (Rupees twenty four lakhs five thousand and eight hundred only) along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled the share of 50% each.
Out of share amount of petitoner No.1 and 2, 40% of the amount together with interest shall be deposited in their names in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank for a period of three years and the remaining 60% of of the amount shall be released to them through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
